coexist-jews.title: Think Israel and a Palestinian state can coexist peacefully: U.S. Jews and Israeli Jews

rows.label: U.S. Jews, 2013
rows.source: Pew Research Center, survey of U.S. Jews (2013), in Comparisons Between Jews in Israel and the U.S.

rows.label: U.S. Jews, 2019–20
rows.source: Pew Research Center, survey of U.S. Jews (n=4,718)

rows.label: Israeli Jews, 2014–15
rows.source: Pew Research Center, Israel religion survey (n=5,601)

coexist-jews.question: A way can be found for Israel and an independent Palestinian state to coexist peacefully (% saying this).
coexist-jews.note: Same Pew wording, different Pew surveys; each bar carries its own survey. Pew's Global Attitudes survey of spring 2014, a different survey from the 2014–15 Israel religion survey, gives 37% for Israeli Jews (https://www.pewresearch.org/wp-content/uploads/sites/20/2026/09/pg_2026.09.15_coexistence_report.pdf). No Pew figure for U.S. Jews on this question after 2020 was found.

coexist-israelis.title: Think Israel and a Palestinian state can coexist peacefully: all Israelis
coexist-israelis.question: A way can be found for Israel and an independent Palestinian state to coexist peacefully (% saying this), all Israeli adults.
coexist-israelis.source: Pew Research Center, Global Attitudes surveys in Israel (trend in the 2026 coexistence report)
coexist-israelis.note: In 2026, 56% of Israelis said it was not possible, the first time a majority said so (Pew). Includes Palestinian citizens of Israel, whom Pew labels "Israeli Arabs"; Pew notes many of them declined to answer in 2026.

self-placement.title: Israeli Jews who place themselves on the right
self-placement.question: Self-placement on a 1–7 left-right scale; 5–7 counted as right.
self-placement.source: Israel Democracy Institute data, via Times of Israel
self-placement.note: The Jewish People Policy Institute found 66% of Israeli Jews placing themselves on the right in July 2026, on a different scale; the two series should not be joined (https://www.timesofisrael.com/battle-for-the-center-large-majority-of-israelis-already-know-how-theyll-vote-poll/).

vote-considerations.title: What Jewish Israelis say will decide their vote
vote-considerations.question: The factor that will most influence which party they vote for, and the second most important factor (first and second choices combined).
vote-considerations.note: IDI's own label for the last item is "judicial reform." Among Arab respondents (150), crime in Arab society led at 53.5%, then the economy at 46%.

paired.note: Two JPPI survey rounds, each row dated. In the August 2025 rows the Israeli figures come from a separate JPPI survey, its Israeli Society Index, fielded earlier that month. JPPI's U.S. sample is a panel of "connected" Jews ("engaged" in the 2026 report), more engaged with Jewish life than U.S. Jews as a whole.
